found.title: swap hides msg.value; with the extra-ETH flag the signer sends more ETH than the amount shown.
found.code: AggregationRouterV4.swap: `if (flags & _REQUIRES_EXTRA_ETH != 0) { require(msg.value > (srcETH ? desc.amount : 0), "Invalid msg.value"); }` and `address(caller).call{value: msg.value}(callData);` Descriptor swap format: fields are desc.amount, desc.minReturnAmount, desc.dstReceiver; `"path": "desc.flags", "visible": "never"`; no `@.value` field.
why: When the extra-ETH flag is set, msg.value can be any amount above desc.amount, or any non-zero amount for an ERC-20 source, and all of it goes to the executor. No field shows msg.value and the flag is hidden, so ETH leaves the wallet in an amount the screen never shows.
The extra-ETH branch accepts and forwards ETH beyond the displayed source amount. Neither the displayed fields nor the intent states this additional payment.
found.fix: Add a field `{"path": "@.value", "label": "ETH sent", "format": "amount"}` with visible always.

found.title: swap shows 'Minimum to Receive', but with the partial-fill flag the signer can receive less.
found.code: AggregationRouterV4.swap: `if (flags & _PARTIAL_FILL != 0) { ... srcToken.uniTransfer(msg.sender, unspentAmount); } require(returnAmount.mul(desc.amount) >= desc.minReturnAmount.mul(spentAmount), ...)` Descriptor: `desc.minReturnAmount` uses `minReceiveAmount` ('Minimum to Receive'); `desc.flags` is `visible: never`.
why: With the partial-fill flag, the code only checks a proportional rate, so the receiver can get less than the 'Minimum to Receive' value shown. The flag is hidden. The unspent source tokens come back to the signer, but the screen shows the minimum as a fixed amount, and partial fills can happen without the signer knowing.
Partial fills enforce a proportional minimum, not the displayed absolute minimum. For example, spending half the source amount permits receiving half the stated minimum; this is not a payout ceiling.
found.fix: Show `desc.flags` bit 0 as a 'Partial fill allowed' field, or change the label to 'Minimum rate (full amount)' and say that unspent input returns to the signer.

found.title: uniswapV3SwapToWithPermit names the sent token from srcToken, but the pool decides which token leaves.
found.code: UnoswapV3Router.uniswapV3SwapToWithPermit: `_permit(address(srcToken), permit); return uniswapV3SwapTo(recipient, amount, minReturn, pools);` and uniswapV3SwapCallback: `token0.safeTransferFrom(payer, msg.sender, uint256(amount0Delta));` / `token1.safeTransferFrom(...)`. Descriptor: field `amount` with `"tokenPath": "srcToken"`.
why: The code uses srcToken only for the permit and never checks it against the pool. The token taken from the signer is token0 or token1 of pools[0], so the screen can name an asset that is not the one taken.
No check binds srcToken to the token pulled by the pool callback. An empty permit and an existing allowance for a different pool token allow that token to leave while the screen names srcToken.
found.fix: Remove tokenPath srcToken from `amount` (show it as unknown token, like uniswapV3SwapTo), or label it 'Token permitted' as a separate field.

found.title: fillContractOrder shows `amount` as takerAsset to sell, but with the maker-amount flag it is makerAsset to receive.
found.code: _fill: `if (takerTraits.isMakingAmount()) { makingAmount = Math.min(amount, remainingMakingAmount); takingAmount = order.calculateTakingAmount(...)`; TakerTraitsLib `_MAKER_AMOUNT_FLAG = 1 << 255`; descriptor fillContractOrder `amount` `$ref fillAmount` ("Amount to sell"), `"tokenPath": "order.takerAsset"`
why: With bit 255 of takerTraits set, amount is the makerAsset amount the signer receives, and the signer pays a computed takingAmount. The screen shows amount as 'Amount to sell' in order.takerAsset. The enum has no key for 128 or higher, so the mode is never stated.
In maker-amount mode, amount specifies purchased makerAsset rather than sold takerAsset. Displaying the full order's amounts does not correct the fill amount's wrong asset and direction.
found.fix: Add enum keys for values with bit 0x80 ("Exact amount to receive") and add a second amount field with tokenPath order.makerAsset, or a label that names both modes.

why: When the _ARGS_HAS_TARGET bit is set, the first 20 bytes of args become the target, and _fill sends the makerAsset (or the unwrapped ETH) to that target. args is visible never, and the enum has no key with bit 8, so the recipient is never shown.
The args target can be a third-party address and receives the purchased makerAsset. Neither the hidden args field nor the displayed order amounts identify that recipient.

found.title: CommitIntent: 'Stake amount' shows the gross deposit, but the platform fee is cut before the stake is locked.
found.code: CommitmentVaultV4._commit: `uint256 fee = _computeFee(token, totalDeposit); ... uint256 netStake = totalDeposit - fee; if (fine > netStake) revert InvalidFine(fine, netStake); ... _storeCommitment(..., netStake, fine, fee, ...); _credit(token, treasury, fee);` and `_computeFee`: `bpsFee = (totalDeposit * platformFeeBps) / 10_000` (platformFeeBps = 100 in the constructor), with minFeeInToken as the floor. CommitmentVaultV5.commitWithSig passes `received` (the full intent.amount) as totalDeposit. Descriptor: field `amount` labelled 'Stake amount' (tokenAmount); the intent 'Open commitment' and n
why: The code keeps the fee for the treasury and locks only totalDeposit minus the fee as the stake. That net stake is what Returned and emergency withdraw pay back, but the screen shows the gross 10 USDC as 'Stake amount' and never mentions a fee. This is the guide's amount rule: a fee rate from storage cuts the amount shown, so it is critical and not the not-critical item 3 (storage values). Also, in case 0 the fine is 10 USDC, which is more than the net stake, so that signed intent would revert with InvalidFine.

Successful commitments lock and refund the deposit minus the platform fee, while the screen labels the gross deposit “Stake amount” without disclosing the deduction. However, case 0 does not demonstrate a successful deduction: its fine equals the deposit, so any positive fee makes it revert.
found.fix: Rename the field to 'Deposit (platform fee deducted)'. Have the intent say a fee is taken, e.g. 'Deposit tokens into a commitment (platform fee: 1% or $1 minimum)'.

found.title: swapBorrowRateMode intent says 'Swap to variable', but rateMode 2 moves debt to stable on Polygon/Avalanche.
found.code: Avalanche/Polygon LendingPool.swapBorrowRateMode: `} else { IVariableDebtToken(reserve.variableDebtTokenAddress).burn(msg.sender, variableDebt, ...); IStableDebtToken(reserve.stableDebtTokenAddress).mint(msg.sender, msg.sender, variableDebt, reserve.currentStableBorrowRate); }`; ValidationLogic.validateSwapRateMode (137/43114): `else if (currentRateMode == DataTypes.InterestRateMode.VARIABLE) { require(variableDebt > 0, ...); /* user wants to swap to stable */ require(stableRateEnabled, ...)`. Descriptor (bound to 137 and 43114): `"intent": "Swap to variable"`, field `rateMode` labelled "Curre
why: On Polygon and Avalanche, rateMode 2 passes validation and turns the signer's variable debt into stable-rate debt, while the title says "Swap to variable". Only mainnet forces the stable-to-variable direction. The action shown is the opposite of the one executed, so this is critical; it does depend on reserve flags in storage (not frozen, stable rate enabled) that the code itself does not rule out.

Polygon and Avalanche permit variable-to-stable conversion when reserve and debt checks pass; mainnet’s STABLE-only restriction does not apply. Showing “Current rate mode: variable” does not disclose the resulting stable debt and contradicts the promised “Swap to variable” outcome.
found.fix: Change the intent to "Swap borrow rate mode" and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Swap {asset} debt from {rateMode} rate".

found.title: scheduleEmissions: the STONX transfer out of the signer's wallet and its amount are not shown
found.code: Ve33Periphery.handleLockData: `(address payer, ...) = abi.decode(data, ...)` with payer = msg.sender from scheduleEmissions; `ACCOUNTANT.payFrom(payer, stakeToken, amount);` -> FlashAccountantLib.payFrom does `transferFrom(from, accountant, amount)`; IVe33 `event EmissionsScheduled(address funder, ..., uint128 amount)`. Descriptor: intent "Schedule Ve33 emissions", fields only Start time, End time, 'Reward rate (Q32)' raw.
why: The signer's STONX (stakeToken 0x570c…, an ERC-20) leaves the wallet by transferFrom, in an amount the contract works out from the rate and the duration. No field shows the amount or says the signer pays, so this effect on the signer's assets is not shown. Only the raw Q32 rate is shown, and that is not the amount transferred.

The periphery pays the schedule’s required tokens from the signer, but the screen only states scheduling times and a rate. The hidden effect is the wallet payment, not merely the raw rate’s readability; the claimed 100 STONX calculation is not verified here.
found.fix: Say it in the intent: "Fund STONX emissions from your wallet". Relabel rewardRate as "STONX per second (Q32 fixed-point)". Add a note that the total paid = rate × (end − start) / 2^32. ERC-7730 cannot compute that product (see the spec-limitation finding).

found.title: burn says the NFT is 'empty', but the code burns any NFT and any remaining stake is lost for good.
found.code: VeToken.sol burn: `function burn(uint256 veId) external payable authorizedForStake(veId) { _burn(veId); _setExtraData(veId, 0); }`; _stakeEndTime: `if (!_exists(veId)) revert TokenDoesNotExist();`; descriptor intent 'Burn empty vote-escrow NFT'
why: burn has no check on ve33.stakeAmount, so it burns an NFT that still holds stake. After the burn, _stakeEndTime reverts with TokenDoesNotExist, so withdrawStake can no longer reach the stake. The intent tells the signer the NFT is empty.

The function burns an authorized NFT without checking that its stake is empty, removing access to any remaining stake through normal withdrawal. The misleading 'empty' assurance is proven, although permanent irrecoverability under every possible remint scenario is not established.
found.fix: Use the intent 'Burn stake NFT {veId}: any STONX or fees still in it are lost forever'.

found.title: cooldownShares restarts the cooldown timer for all USDe the signer already has pending; nothing shown says so.
found.code: StakedUSDeV2.cooldownShares: `cooldowns[msg.sender].cooldownEnd = uint104(block.timestamp) + cooldownDuration; cooldowns[msg.sender].underlyingAmount += uint152(assets);` and StakedUSDeV2.unstake pays out the whole `userCooldown.underlyingAmount` only `if (block.timestamp >= userCooldown.cooldownEnd ...)`. Screen (case 0): intent 'Cooldown Shares', field 'Amount: 1515266.436573198420501508 sUSDe'.
why: Each account has one cooldown record. The new USDe is added to it and the single end time is reset to now plus the full duration, so USDe already pending cannot be claimed until the new end time. This is like the calibrated 'existing stake folded into new delegation' critical. The screen shows only the intent and the new amount, and nothing on the not-critical list covers the change to the existing pending position.

A successful call resets the deadline for the entire pending balance, including earlier USDe; no guard excludes existing cooldowns. This changes an existing withdrawal right, not merely an undisplayable duration, and the screen states only the new amount.
found.fix: Change the intent to 'Unstake sUSDe; restarts any pending cooldown' or add a notice that the cooldown resets for all pending USDe.

found.title: cooldownAssets restarts the cooldown timer for all USDe the signer already has pending; nothing shown says so.
found.code: StakedUSDeV2.cooldownAssets: `cooldowns[msg.sender].cooldownEnd = uint104(block.timestamp) + cooldownDuration; cooldowns[msg.sender].underlyingAmount += uint152(assets);` Descriptor: intent 'Cooldown Assets', only field `#.assets` 'Amount'.
why: This has the same code as cooldownShares. Any pending USDe joins the same record, and its end time is pushed back to now plus cooldownDuration (max 90 days). The intent and the Amount field do not say that USDe already in cooldown gets locked again.

A successful call resets the same deadline governing all previously pending USDe, without checking whether a cooldown already exists. The descriptor shows only the new assets amount and does not disclose the effect on the earlier withdrawal position.
found.fix: Change the intent to 'Unstake sUSDe; restarts any pending cooldown' or add a notice about the reset.

found.title: LeveragedOrder Open action borrows sellAmount+feeAmount as new debt; nothing on screen says borrow or debt.
found.code: LeverageRfqEngine.sol _openLeverage: `uint256 totalBorrow = order.sellAmount + order.feeAmount; ... pm.borrowFlashAndDepositFor(user, order.sellToken, totalBorrow, order.buyToken, order.buyAmount, ...)`. Descriptor: intent "Sign spot order", interpolatedIntent "Spot sell {sellAmount}", field label "Sell", enum 0 → "Open"
why: A signed OPEN order makes the PositionsManager borrow sellAmount+feeAmount against the user and deposit the bought token as collateral, so the signer takes on new debt. The screen calls it a spot sale and shows only the bare label "Open". Nothing mentions a borrow, debt or leverage, and the domain name is not displayed. No not-critical case covers this, so it is critical.
Open authorizes borrowing sellAmount plus feeAmount for the user. Showing those amounts as Sell and Fee, with Action Open, does not disclose debt under an explicit spot-order intent.
found.fix: State the action-specific effect, e.g. an intent like "Leveraged order: borrow and sell {sellAmount}", and label the amount "Borrow & sell" with a note that the fee is borrowed too. Or split descriptors or text per action if the wallet supports that.

Descriptor: "Spot sell {sellAmount}", label "Minimum buy", enum 1 → "Close"
why: A CLOSE order takes the sold tokens out of the signer's position collateral, not from the wallet. The bought tokens repay the signer's debt instead of reaching the wallet. The screen shows a spot sale with a "Minimum buy" as if it were received, so the positions that change are shown differently. One caveat: the PositionsManager source is not in the directory, so the repay behaviour rests on the function name and this contract's own doc comment.

Close authorizes collateral withdrawal and debt repayment, rather than a spot sale delivering purchased tokens to the wallet. The bare Close label does not disclose those position effects under the spot-order intent.

found.code: PurchaseBundler.sol executeOperation: `uint256 owed = amounts[i] + premiums[i]; ... if (balance < owed) { asset.safeTransferFrom(_buyer, address(this), owed - balance); }`. Mined effect in case 3: WETH transfer of 29828106748804350315 from 0x8463…33f2 (the signer) to 0xf46a…6feb, marked signer "out". Screen in case 3: only `Flash loan: 29.813200148729985322 WETH`, `Flash loan pool: 0x8787…A4E2` and `Value sent: 3.836799851270014678 ETH`. No field shows a WETH pull from the signer.
why: I could not refute this. In executeOperation, any shortfall between the flash-loan debt and the bundler's balance is pulled from the signer's wallet by transferFrom. In case 3 this pulled 29.828106748804350315 WETH, which is the 29.8132 WETH flash loan plus its premium. Nothing on the screen says this. The screen shows only the flash-loan amount from the pool, without the premium, and says the signer receives the new loan ("Principal receiver: 0x8463…33f2"). It does not say that WETH then leaves the signer's wallet. No item on the not-critical list covers this. The amount is not unreadable or shown through another field, the payer is not the contract, and the amount pulled is not capped by the new loan's principal.

Case 3 proves the bundler pulls 29.828106748804350315 WETH from the signer after the new loan pays them. The displayed flash-loan principal does not disclose this wallet debit; “You pay” covers separate swap inputs and is absent from this case’s screen.

found.code: WstethStaker.sol, WstETHReferralStaker.stakeETH: `uint256 wstETHAmount = wstETH.wrap(stethAmount); wstETH.transfer(msg.sender, wstETHAmount);`. descriptor.json: `"intent": "Stake ETH", "interpolatedIntent": "Stake {@.value}"`, and the only visible field is `"label": "Amount to stake", "path": "@.value"`. cases/0.json mined: WSTETH 12597855047834535196 to the signer, `"signer": "in"`.
why: stakeETH always wraps the stETH it gets and sends the signer wstETH, never stETH. The case 0 trace shows the signer receives 12.597855047834535196 WSTETH for 15.49 ETH. The screen shows only "Stake ETH", "Stake 15.49 ETH" and "Amount to stake". The descriptor's contractName mentions wstETH, but the case screen does not show it, and nothing on screen says which token arrives. The blind reader expected about 15.49 stETH. The guide calls a different asset critical even when the value is the same. No item on the not-critical list covers this: the wrap is not stated anywhere, so it is not the prerequisite of a named action.

The function wraps stETH and sends wstETH to the signer, confirmed by the mined receipt of 12.597855047834535196 WSTETH. The screen never identifies the received asset; the metadata contract name does not appear on the supplied screen.

found.title: vaultBundlesV1Deposit hides maxSharePriceE27, the only bound on how few vault shares the signer receives.
found.code: VaultBundlesV1.sol, vaultBundlesV1Deposit: `uint256 shares = IERC4626(vault).deposit(toDeposit, msg.sender); require(toDeposit.mulDivUp(1e27, shares) <= maxSharePriceE27, SlippageExceeded());`. Descriptor: `{"label": "Max share price", "path": "#.maxSharePriceE27", "visible": "never"}`. Case 0 screen shows only Vault, "Base units, with fee" 2000000000, Referral fee 0% and Deadline, while the signer receives 1917030928050759063648 gtusdcp.
why: The signer chooses maxSharePriceE27 in calldata, and it is the only check on how few shares the vault mints to them. The descriptor hides it with `visible: never`, and no field shows the shares or a minimum. This matches the guide's critical example "how little may come back, is not shown". It is not covered by not-critical #6 (that case is `visible: optional`) or #3 (this is a calldata bound, not a value read from storage).

The hidden calldata parameter sets the minimum acceptable shares for the deposited assets. No other displayed field states that bound; the exception for outputs derived by the vault does not cover this explicit input limit.
found.fix: Make `#.maxSharePriceE27` visible. Use the label "Max share price (assets per share, 1e27 scale)" and the format `raw`, or a `unit` format if one fits. Leave it out of `interpolatedIntent`.

Descriptor: `{"label": "Max share price", "path": "#.destMaxSharePriceE27", "visible": "never"}`. Case 7 screen shows From vault, To vault, "Shares to move" 0.04033210861146132 gtWETHc, Referral fee and Deadline, while the signer receives 41832542822934993 gtwethb.
why: destMaxSharePriceE27 is the only calldata bound on how many destination-vault shares the signer receives, and the descriptor hides it with `visible: never`. No field shows the shares received or a minimum, so the screen does not state how little may come back. This is critical under the severity guide, and no not-critical case applies.

found.fix: Make `#.destMaxSharePriceE27` visible with the label "Max share price at destination (1e27 scale)" and the format `raw`. Leave it out of `interpolatedIntent`.

found.title: dagSwapByOrderId: a from-token commission in trailing calldata takes extra tokens beyond Amount to Send.
found.code: DexRouter.dagSwapTo: `_doCommissionFromToken(commissionInfo, msg.sender, receiver, baseRequest.fromTokenAmount, ...)`; CommissionLib._doCommissionFromTokenInternal: `let amount := div(mul(inputAmount, rate), sub(DENOMINATOR, totalRate))` then `_claimToken(token, payer, referrer, amount)`. Descriptor dagSwapByOrderId shows only `baseRequest.fromTokenAmount` as Amount to Send.
why: dagSwapByOrderId calls dagSwapTo. When the trailing calldata carries a from-token commission flag, the router pulls an extra amount from the signer on top of fromTokenAmount. No field shows this commission. _validateCommissionInfo only blocks it for the NO_TRANSFER, BY_INVEST and PERMIT2 modes, not for the legacy mode.
The legacy transfer path charges the commission separately from the displayed swap input. Commission validation permits this path.

found.title: swapWrap: the enum labels first byte 0x01 as WETH to ETH, but the code wraps ETH.

found.title: mintWithAttestation shows depositTokenAmount, but with USDon as deposit token it takes quantity times price instead.
found.code: GMTokenManager.sol mintWithAttestation: `uint256 mintUSDonValue = (quote.quantity * quote.price) / GM_NORMALIZER;` ... `if (depositToken == address(usdon)) { IERC20(usdon).safeTransferFrom(_msgSender(), address(this), mintUSDonValue); }`. depositTokenAmount is only used in the else branch. Descriptor: field `depositTokenAmount` 'Deposit Amount' (tokenAmount, tokenPath depositToken); `quote.price` has `visible: never`; interpolatedIntent 'Mint {quote.quantity} using {depositTokenAmount}'.
why: When the deposit token is USDon, the contract ignores depositTokenAmount and takes quantity*price USDon from the signer. Both values come from calldata, and the price is hidden. So the screen states the amount that leaves the wallet as a different value from the one the code moves. This is not in the not-critical list: the price is a calldata value, not a storage value, and the shown amount is not an unused zero alternative.

The USDon branch ignores depositTokenAmount and charges quantity × price / GM_NORMALIZER, without checking equality to the displayed deposit. The descriptor hides price and supplies no other field showing the actual USDon payment.
found.fix: Show `quote.price` (for example format `unit`, base USD, decimals 18, label 'Price per GM Token'), and relabel the deposit field 'Deposit Amount (USDon: quantity x price)'. Add a test case with depositToken = USDon.

found.title: redeemWithAttestation shows a minimum received that the code does not check when receiveToken is USDon.
found.code: GMTokenManager.sol redeemWithAttestation: `if (receiveToken == address(usdon)) { IERC20(usdon).safeTransfer(_msgSender(), redemptionUSDonValue); } else { ... usdonManager.redeem(redemptionUSDonValue, receiveToken, minimumReceiveAmount); ... }`. NatSpec: 'ONLY applicable if the user requests a non-USDon token'. Descriptor: 'Min Receive Amount' (minimumReceiveAmount) and 'Redeem {quote.quantity} for {minimumReceiveAmount}+'; `quote.price` has `visible: never`.
why: On the USDon path, the code never checks minimumReceiveAmount. The signer receives quantity*price, which comes from the hidden quote.price, and this can be less than the minimum the screen promises. The screen states a minimum received that the code does not enforce, and the real amount is not shown anywhere. That means how little may come back is shown wrong.

The USDon branch burns the GM tokens and pays the quote-derived amount without enforcing minimumReceiveAmount. A minimum above that payment remains unchecked, contradicting the displayed minimum; this is not a capped withdrawal or merely unreadable information.
found.fix: Show `quote.price` (format `unit`, base USD, decimals 18, label 'Price per GM Token') so the USDon amount is checkable, and relabel the minimum 'Min Receive (not applied for USDon)'. Add a test case with receiveToken = USDon.

found.title: Order: maker relayer and protocol fees taken from the signer are hidden, so the price shown is not what the signer nets or pays.
found.code: WyvernExchangeWithBulkCancellations.sol executeFundsTransfer: `if (sell.makerRelayerFee > 0) { uint makerRelayerFee = SafeMath.div(SafeMath.mul(sell.makerRelayerFee, price), INVERSE_BASIS_POINT); ... transferTokens(sell.paymentToken, sell.maker, sell.feeRecipient, makerRelayerFee);` and buy side `transferTokens(sell.paymentToken, buy.maker, buy.feeRecipient, makerRelayerFee)`; descriptor: `{"path": "makerRelayerFee", "label": "Maker Relayer Fee", "visible": "never"}`, `{"path": "feeRecipient", ... "visible": "never"}`; case 0 screen: `Price: 7.5 WETH`, and the message has makerRelayerFee "250"
why: The maker fee rate and the fee recipient are fields of the signed order, not values from storage. On the SplitFee path, executeFundsTransfer sends price*makerRelayerFee/10000 of the payment token from the signer (the maker) to feeRecipient. In case 0 (feeMethod 1 = SplitFee, side Sell, makerRelayerFee 250, WETH) that is 0.1875 WETH, so the signer nets 7.3125 WETH, not the 7.5 WETH shown. The descriptor marks makerRelayerFee, makerProtocolFee and feeRecipient `visible: never`, and no other field or the intent mentions a fee. The guide's examples list 'amount minus a fee, full amount shown' as critical, and not-critical item 3 does not apply because the fee rate comes from the signed order, not from storage.

Settlement charges maker fees that no displayed field states; valid sell orders lose fees from proceeds, and buy orders pay them additionally. Case 0 has no mined transaction and zero protocol fees, so 7.3125 WETH describes the fee calculation, not a verified receipt.
found.fix: Show makerRelayerFee and makerProtocolFee as fields (a bps/percentage label such as 'Maker fee (bps of price)'), and show feeRecipient as an addressName 'Fee recipient'.

found.code: RaribleTransferManager.doTransfersWithFees: `rest = transferRoyalties(paymentSide.asset.assetType, nftSide.asset.assetType, nftSide.payouts, rest, paymentSide.asset.value, paymentSide.from, paymentSide.proxy);` … `transferPayouts(paymentSide.asset.assetType, rest, ...)`; getRoyaltiesByAssetType: `return royaltiesRegistry.getRoyalties(token, tokenId);`; screen case 0: {"label": "Take asset amount", "value": "75000000000000000"}

found.title: batchExecute: calls[].value (native currency leaving the Safe) is never its own field; empty-data transfers have no inner descriptor
found.code: BatchExecutor.sol batchExecute: `(bool success, bytes memory errorData) = calls[i].to.call{value: calls[i].value}(calls[i].data);` and line 53 `if (calls[i].to.code.length == 0 && calls[i].data.length > 0) revert` (this only blocks data sent to EOAs, so a call with empty data to any address goes through). descriptor.json batchExecute: the only field is `{"path": "calls.[].data", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "calls.[].to", "amountPath": "calls.[].value"}}`
why: The contract runs in the Safe through delegatecall and sends `calls[i].value` of the Safe's native currency to `calls[i].to`. Nothing in the code limits that value. The descriptor has no field for `calls.[].value`. `amountPath` only passes the value to an inner descriptor, which under the spec 'MAY reference' `@.value`, and the spec's fallback when no inner descriptor matches shows only a calldata hash and the callee. A plain transfer with empty data has no selector, so no inner descriptor exists and nothing on screen shows the amount. This matches the guide's critical example of native currency leaving in an amount never shown, and the not-critical cases do not cover it: the amount is not shown anywhere else, and it is a fact, not a possibility.

An empty-data call with nonzero value transfers the Safe’s native currency without displaying its amount. The fallback can show the recipient, so the recipient-omission claim is overstated, but the hidden amount confirms the critical finding.
found.fix: Add per-call fields: `calls.[].to` labelled 'To' (addressName) and `calls.[].value` labelled 'Value' (format amount). Keep the calldata field.

found.title: withdraw shows 'Withdraw exactly X USDe', but the receiver gets sUSDe
found.code: AllocatorVaultV3.withdraw: `uint256 assets = strategy.previewWithdraw(_underlying); ... if (config.hasCooldown) { IERC20(address(strategy)).safeTransfer(receiver, assets); }`. descriptor.json withdraw field: `"path": "_underlying", "label": "Withdraw exactly", "format": "tokenAmount", "params": {"token": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingToken"}` (USDe 0x4c9E…8B3). Mined case 1 (redeem, same `config.hasCooldown` branch): 1626.31 sUSDe (0x9d39…3497) sent from the vault to the signer.
why: The screen says the receiver gets exactly X USDe. With hasCooldown on, which the mined redeem shows, the receiver instead gets previewWithdraw(X) sUSDe, a different asset and a different number, and no USDe at all. The storage-value exception in the severity guide applies: the stored flag changes what the signer receives against the amount shown, so this is critical.
The cooldown branch sends sUSDe instead of the USDe explicitly promised by “Withdraw exactly.” Case 1 establishes this branch’s actual output asset; no withdrawal field explains the substitution.
found.fix: Change the intent to "Withdraw sUSDe worth USDe amount". Change the label to 'USDe value to withdraw (paid in sUSDe)'. You can also add a constant field 'Receive asset: sUSDe'.
